payload.name: Search travel events for city-enumeration questions
payload.description: When a question asks which cities/places a person visited or mentioned visiting, even to another person, search travel/event memories and do not require the audience name or the word 'visit'.
content: If a question enumerates cities/places a person visited or mentioned visiting (e.g., 'Which US cities does X mention visiting to Y?'), run at least one hybrid search combining the person's name with travel/event terms such as 'traveled to', 'visited', 'event in', 'trip to', and 'favorite city'; do not require the audience's name or the word 'mention' to appear.

Treat event memories that locate the person in a city (upcoming games, trips, visits, 'favorite city to explore') as evidence for city visitation even when the memory does not name the audience or use the word 'visit'.
Before answering with a city list, run a supplementary search for each already-found city paired with the person's name to catch additional city memories the first query missed.

solves: Search over-anchored on the audience and the surface verb 'visiting', so a city memory stored as an event (e.g., an upcoming game in a favorite city) was never retrieved. The reusable fix is to retrieve the person's travel/event memories independently of the audience when a question enumerates cities/places visited or mentioned visiting. This applies to future 'which cities did X visit/mention to Y' questions where location evidence may live in event memories without the audience's name.
